yaml.title: MOVICI
yaml.subtitle: Modelling Online Vigilance and Institutions in the Communication of Information

markdown.markdown:
MOVICI is a research programme examining how people search for, evaluate, learn from, and exchange information in digital and social environments. Its central concern is **epistemic vigilance**: how people decide what deserves attention, trust, verification, epistemic credit, and integration into knowledge. The programme combines a theoretical framework (**CAVL — Cognitive Architecture for Vigilant Learning**), empirical studies of **open Web search** and **cooperative or competitive debate**, and an **agent-based model** exploring how local learning and credit-allocation mechanisms can generate cumulative trajectories over repeated interactions. Across these studies, MOVICI connects prior knowledge, metacognition, information search, source evaluation, expertise recognition, epistemic credit, social interaction, and socially structured opportunities to learn.
WORKING PAPER 01
### [CAVL: A Cognitive Architecture for Vigilant Learning](working-papers/wp01-cavl/index.qmd) A theoretical architecture for understanding socially embedded vigilant learning.
WORKING PAPER 02
### [Prior Knowledge and Learning from Open Web Search](working-papers/wp02-information-search/index.qmd) How prior knowledge, search activity, source evaluation, and learning interact during open Web search.
WORKING PAPER 03
### [Epistemic Credit in Cooperative and Competitive Debate](working-papers/wp03-debate/index.qmd) How cooperation and competition shape epistemic credit, calibration, and expertise recognition.
WORKING PAPER 04
### [Learning from Documents and from Others: Knowledge Change and Epistemic Coordination](working-papers/wp04-search-debate/index.qmd) A within-participant comparison of learning from Web documents and learning through debate.
WORKING PAPER 05
### [Misallocation of Epistemic Credit in Socially Embedded Learning: An Empirically Anchored Agent-Based Model of Information Search and Debate](working-papers/wp05-agent-based-model/index.qmd) An empirically anchored agent-based model of information search, debate, epistemic credit, and cumulative learning.
## MOVICI Video Series The five working papers are accompanied by accessible video presentations.
